newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA PROMISE GOAL FEAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA PROMISE GOAL FEAST.

text.p: Spanish soccer fans await Atletico Madrid's league game with Barcelona this weekend as if it were the latest instalment of an action-packed thriller series.

The five League, Spanish Cup and Super Cup ties between the two this season have already clocked up an amazing 30 goals at an average of six per game. Over the last 18 Atletico-Barca meetings the average has been five.
The season kicked off with a 6-5 aggregate Spanish Super Cup win for Barcelona.
Barcelona then scraped a 3-3 draw in a high-quality league match at the Camp Nou in November which was followed by a 2-2 draw in the Cup quarter-final first leg.
However, the best was yet to come.
In one of the most extraordinary games ever played in Spain, Barcelona launched a dramatic second-half comeback to win the second leg cup game 5-4 after trailing 3-0 in the opening 30 minutes.
For Milinko Pantic, who scored all four Atletico goals, the game was particularly bitter-sweet.
The defeat marked the beginning of the end for last season's double winners Atletico, whose league form suffered around the time of a European Cup quarter-final defeat by Ajax Amsterdam.
"No Atletico fan can be happy with what's happened," said club owner Jesus Gil.
But if revenge and helping to secure a UEFA Cup place for next season are all that Gil can realistically hope for from Sunday's encounter, for Barcelona the stakes are much higher.
With 10 games left to play, Bobby Robson's side trail leaders Real Madrid by seven points.
Barcelona face their arch-rivals on May 10 and must also deal with Real Betis and Deportivo Coruna -- third and fourth respectively -- in the home stretch.

A slip-up in the Vicente Calderon stadium could not only give valuable breathing space to Real Madrid but also damage Barcelona's hopes of securing second place, and with it access to the European Cup.
Barcelona's European Cup Winners' Cup campaign this season suffered a setback on Thursday when the club was held 1-1 at home by Italy's Fiorentina in the semifinal first leg.
The Spaniards clearly missed the energy and commitment of injured defenders Luis Enrique Martinez and Sergi Barjuan in that game.
But two other notable absentees from Thursday -- playmakers Josep Guardiola and Ivan de la Pena -- will retake their places after serving a one-game suspension from European competition.
